requirement_text.REQ-051:
Port src/engine/transition.zig's PARALLEL_GATEWAY branches (per src/design/engine.md "Section EE-06: Parallel Split", L2638 and "Section EE-07: Parallel Join", L2898) into REQ-044's transition dispatch. Pure, no I/O, same contract as REQ-044. Split and join ship together because they share the Token/JoinCounter model and neither is independently meaningful.
SPLIT (EE-06):
- A token reaching a PARALLEL_GATEWAY with N outgoing edges produces N independent tokens simultaneously, one per edge, each with its own branch_id (EE-06 AC1).
- Each token progresses independently: a task completion on one branch never blocks another (EE-06 AC2).
- The split emits a PendingEvent recording the split (EE-06 AC3), and all N tokens are created in one transaction at the persistence layer (EE-06 AC4 / DB-03 -- the atomicity is REQ-047's orchestration job, the token production is this requirement's).
JOIN (EE-07):
- A PARALLEL_GATEWAY acting as a join waits until all ACTIVE incoming tokens have arrived before creating the single outgoing token (EE-07 AC1), tracked via transition.zig's JoinCounter struct (received_count/expected_from_branches, added by R-Co's ISS-105).
- "Active" EXCLUDES tokens on branches cancelled via REQ-052's EE-08 path: a cancelled branch contributes no token and is excluded from the join count, so the join still fires when the remaining active branches arrive (EE-07 AC2/AC3). This exclusion is the single subtlest rule in the parallel model -- a naive implementation waits forever.
- If ALL branches of a split are cancelled before any reaches the join, the join node is itself cancelled and the instance transitions to CANCELLED (EE-07 AC4).
- The join fires EXACTLY ONCE regardless of concurrent token arrival order (EE-07 AC5).
- Variable key collisions between branches merging at the join follow REQ-049's EE-09 collision policy (overwrite plus VARIABLE_OVERWRITTEN event) -- reuse it, do not write a second merge rule.

IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE (confirmed by ORCH before dispatch): REQ-052 (instance cancellation, still pending) is NOT a dependency of this requirement. REQ-052's own requirements.yaml entry states explicitly: "That token-level rule [cancelled-branch exclusion] lives in REQ-051's pure transition logic; this requirement [REQ-052] owns the instance-level persistence of a cancellation." This means REQ-051 must itself define whatever data representation marks a token/branch as cancelled (e.g. a token status or a cancelled-branch-ids set on InstanceState) -- purely, with no I/O -- and the join logic reads that representation. REQ-052 will later be the caller-initiated path that sets it via real persistence; you do not need REQ-052 to exist to design or implement this. Do not block on it; do not silently invent instance-level persistence to compensate for it (that's out of scope -- REQ-047/052's job).

task.description:
Design REQ-051: PARALLEL_GATEWAY split and join in Letflow.Engine.Transition's pure dispatch (lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex), matching R-Co's transition.zig EE-06/EE-07 sections (see requirement_text above for the exact behavioral contract, and c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\src\engine\transition.zig and src\design\engine.md if reachable from this environment for the original port source -- if unreachable, work from the requirement_text's own description, which is a faithful summary). Read lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex, instance_state.ex, and token.ex in full first, plus req044's and req049's own design docs for this module's established conventions (dispatch function shape, PendingEvent representation, purity discipline, how REQ-049's merge policy is invoked).

Design must cover: (1) Token.branch_id generation/uniqueness for a split producing N tokens; (2) how a join's JoinCounter (received_count/expected_from_branches) is represented in InstanceState -- pure data, no process/GenServer; (3) the cancelled-branch representation this requirement itself must introduce (per the scope note above) and how the join's active-token count excludes it; (4) the all-branches-cancelled -> join-cancelled -> instance CANCELLED path; (5) exactly-once join firing under concurrent arrival order; (6) reuse (not reimplementation) of REQ-049's variable merge/collision policy at the join.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc(s) at lib/letflow/design/ (following req044/req049's naming convention) cover every one of REQ-051's 6 acceptance criteria with a concrete design element.
Design explicitly specifies the new cancelled-branch/token representation this requirement introduces (do not defer it to REQ-052 -- REQ-052 depends on it existing).
Design explicitly reuses REQ-049's merge-policy function rather than defining a second collision rule.
Design stays within Transition's pure, no-I/O contract (no Ecto/Repo calls).
Open questions listed explicitly rather than silently resolved.

result.summary: Produced lib/letflow/design/req051-parallel-gateway-split-join.md covering EE-06 split and EE-07 join. New Letflow.Engine.JoinCounter struct (join_node_id, origin_token_id, expected_from_branches/received_from_branches/cancelled_branches as MapSet(String.t())) added, keyed by join_node_id on a new InstanceState.join_counters field -- this is the concrete cancelled-branch representation REQ-051 itself introduces (via a new {:cancel_branch, branch_id} transition_event/0 constructor and its own pure dispatch), not deferred to REQ-052. Split: dispatch_parallel_split/4 produces N child tokens from a PARALLEL_GATEWAY's out-edges, id/branch_id derived deterministically as parent_token_id<>"/"<>declaration_order_index (never edge.id, since no structural check guarantees edge-id uniqueness) -- necessary because transition/3 cannot call :rand/:crypto and must stay deterministic. A find_matching_join/2 graph walk locates the corresponding join node at split time and seeds its JoinCounter. Join: dispatch_parallel_join/4 plus a shared join_outcome/1 helper (:wait | :fire | :cancel_join, a pure function of the JoinCounter's 3 sets) drive both token-arrival and branch-cancellation dispatch through one decision point -- fire excludes cancelled branches from the wait set (EE-07 AC2/AC3), all-cancelled-with-zero-arrivals triggers :cancel_join -> instance status :cancelled (EE-07 AC4), and Map.delete-ing the cohort on any fire/cancel outcome plus join_outcome/1's pure set-algebra together give exactly-once, order-independent firing (EE-07 AC5). REQ-049's VariableMerge.merge/3 is called (not reimplemented) at every join-fire; documented explicitly as a no-op today given InstanceState has no per-branch variable overlay, flagged as an open question (12.5) rather than silently invented. transition_error/0 gains 3 variants, pending_event/0 is narrowed from REQ-044's term() placeholder to a real 3-constructor union. No implementation code, no Repo/Logger/clock/:rand/:crypto calls -- pure, no-I/O, matching REQ-044's contract. 8 open questions listed explicitly (12.1-12.5 plus 3.2/3.3/4.1's inline flags), none silently resolved. Noted in issues: handoff's artifacts_in names lib/letflow/design/req049-variable-scoping-merge.md, which does not exist -- the actual file is req049-variable-merge.md (read and used instead).
